method: Read directly with curl: thetrail.ca (passes, the-trails, about), ofsc.on.ca news/FAQ, bancroft.ca trail pages, northernontario.travel articles, ontario.ca (Crown land FAQ, Lingham Lake CR statement). Everything else is from WebSearch summaries; ofatv.org, quintenews, frontenacnews, countyofrenfrew, haliburtoncounty, parktoparktrail, limericklake, chatvc and discoverbancroft were blocked here. The app's geometry was cross-checked against the LIO Ontario Trail Network (OTN) layer in data/lio/otn_trails.geojson. 'Unknown' means no source was found.

trails.name: Hastings Heritage Trail
trails.pass: EOTA pass: ATV/dirt bike $150 season, $75 week, $25 day (thetrail.ca online form, read 2026-11-14). The Town of Bancroft page still says $20/day, which is out of date. An OFATV permit is also honoured on this trail under the 2021 EOTA-OFATV MOU (Hastings County trails only).
trails.season: Officially four-season and open all year (Town of Bancroft, EOTA). But a Limerick Lake Lodge page (map updated 2025-10-13) says wheeled-vehicle use is prohibited until the end of the 2025/26 snowmobile season. That is one source and is unconfirmed. In winter the corridor also carries OFSC TOP E106/B106E.
trails.notes: OTN lists ATV and off-road motorcycle as permitted uses. Consider a winter (Dec to Apr) caution in the app.

trails.name: Trans Canada Trail (Hastings County section: Glen Ross - Stirling area - Tweed - Kaladar, about 75-80 km)
trails.pass: EOTA pass, or an OFATV permit (the 2021 MOU names 'the Trans Canada Rail trail that stretches across Hastings County east to west')
trails.notes: This is the EOTA-managed former CP corridor. EOTA's own 'Central Hastings Heritage Loop' ATV route runs on it west of Tweed. Ontario Trails says the Kaladar section is 'part of Eastern Ontario Trail Alliance and there is user pay'. The app's NO comes from the generic TCT/OTN attribute, which lists only hiking, cycling and skiing. The about 18 km west of Glen Ross (Trent Hills, lon -77.78 to -77.6) were not verified, so mark that part UNSURE.

trails.name: Central Frontenac Trailway (TCT, Arden/Kennebec - Sharbot Lake, about 38 km in app)
trails.app_class: NO (12.4 km + part of the TCT km above)
trails.pass: Probably EOTA. The Verona & District ATV Club has a use arrangement (2021).
trails.notes: Central Frontenac owns these 30 km and EOTA administers them (Frontenac News, 2021-06-30). The MOU covered EOTA restoring the trail and an arrangement with VATVC 'on its use'. OTN lists no ATV use. No source says ATVs are banned. A forum report says EOTA lacked a user agreement near Sharbot Lake at some point.

trails.name: Egan Creek Trail
trails.correct_class: MAYBE if it is the EOTA trail; ROAD only if it is an assumed township road
trails.pass: EOTA (per OTN association)
trails.notes: OTN lists it as an Eastern Ontario Trails Alliance multi-use trail (7.9 km) that permits ATVs. The app tags it as a Tudor & Cashel road. Check whether OSM's 'Egan Creek Trail' is a municipal road. No web source names this trail.

trails.name: Old Bessemer Trail
trails.app_class: Not in the named list. About 2 km is named; the rest is mapped as Bessemer Road / Egan Creek Road Network (ROAD/FREE).
trails.pass: EOTA (per OTN)
trails.notes: OTN lists it as an EOTA multi-use trail (10.6 km) that permits ATVs. The app covers about 78% of it under road or forest-road names, so it gets FREE/ROAD instead of a pass flag. No web source found.

trails.name: Limerick Trail
trails.app_class: Not named. The geometry is St. Ola Road plus unnamed segments.
trails.correct_class: MAYBE where off-road; ROAD on St. Ola Road
trails.pass: EOTA (per OTN)
trails.notes: OTN lists it as an EOTA trail (24 km) that permits ATVs. Most of it overlaps St. Ola Road in the app, so it is probably an on-road EOTA connector.

trails.name: Coe Hill Siderail
trails.app_class: MAYBE (as 'Brinklow to Coe Hill Trail', 10.2 km)
trails.pass: EOTA (per OTN); an OFATV permit may also apply under the Hastings County MOU (not confirmed for this spur)
trails.notes: The geometry is fully present under a different name.

trails.name: Weslemkoon Lake Multi-Use Trail
trails.pass: EOTA (per OTN)
trails.notes: OTN lists it as an EOTA trail (23.6 km) that permits ATVs. The earlier survey's 'free Crown land Weslemkoon loop' does not match the EOTA designation. Leave the surrounding MNRF roads FREE but keep the designated trail as MAYBE. Ontario Trails' 'Weslemkoon Lake Trail' is a scenic driving route, not an ATV trail.

trails.name: Trail of Two Lakes
trails.pass: EOTA (per OTN)
trails.notes: OTN permitted uses include ATV and off-road motorcycle.

trails.name: E100 & E102 / E105 / East-West / Trail 101, 105, 153 / 'Multiuse Trail' (EOTA multi-use trails)
trails.notes: OTN lists them all under EOTA with ATV permitted. E100/E102 geometry exists in the app under OSM names (Barry Lake Trail, Norcan Trail, Stagecoach Rd).

trails.name: E104 Trail / Bytown Motorcycle Trails (92.6 km) / K&P Trail (BMA part)
trails.pass: Bytown Motorcycle Association; whether membership is needed is unknown
trails.notes: OTN lists the only permitted use on every BMA trail as 'Off-Road Motorcycle'. BMA is a dirt-bike club (Trailforks directory). If the app covers dirt bikes, keep MAYBE for that vehicle class. Medium confidence.

trails.name: Old Hastings Road
trails.app_class: ROAD (about 32 km: Tudor & Cashel by-law; Wollaston/Limerick under the O. Reg. 8/03 default) + 'Old Hastings Road Network N/S of Hwy 620' FREE (28 km MNRF roads)
trails.correct_class: ROAD / FREE (by-law details are with the other agent)
trails.pass: No trail pass required in any source
trails.season: Unknown. Parts are seasonal or unmaintained.
trails.notes: A 2023 Northern Ontario Travel feature describes riding about 45 km by ATV from Hwy 62 south of Bancroft to Hwy 62 near Millbridge, with no pass. Access is directly from the Hastings Heritage Trail at Ormsby.

trails.name: Park-To-Park Trail
trails.pass: Park to Park Trail Association pass. The EOTA OnePass also covers it (2022 article and 2020 OFATV infographic). 2026 price unknown.
trails.notes: OTN permitted uses include ATV and off-road motorcycle.

trails.name: Ottawa Valley Recreational Trail - Algonquin Trail
trails.pass: OFATV permit (choose Renfrew County ATV Club) or OFTR permit, plus licence and insurance. 2026 price unknown.
trails.season: May 1 - Nov 30 (County of Renfrew FAQ / RCATV lease)

trails.name: JR Booth Heritage Railway Trail (Whitney - Madawaska - Wilno)
trails.app_class: MAYBE 64.5 km (EOTA); NO 4.1 km (Upper Madawaska River PP); MAYBE 0.7 km
trails.correct_class: MAYBE; the 4.1 km NO is UNSURE
trails.pass: Permit required for motorized users (Ontario Nature Trails). EOTA sells passes in Whitney, Madawaska and Wilno. Which permit applies is unknown.
trails.notes: Part of it is also OFSC trail B in winter. Whether ORVs may use the rail bed through Upper Madawaska River Provincial Park was not confirmed.

trails.name: K&P Trail
trails.correct_class: MAYBE (NO south of Bellrock Rd in Frontenac County)
trails.pass: Frontenac section: Frontenac ATV Club (OFATV) or EOTA permit, though the county's own pages conflict. Renfrew section: OFATV/RCATV. MVCA section (Snow Road - Barryvale): OTN lists ATV.
trails.season: Frontenac: early April (after thaw) - Nov 30. Renfrew: May 1 - Nov 30.
trails.notes: The Frontenac part is mostly outside about 100 km of Bancroft.

trails.name: Haliburton County Rail Trail (Kinmount - Haliburton)
trails.app_class: Not found by name in app geometry
trails.pass: HATVA or KATVA permit (reciprocal); 2026 price unknown
trails.season: May 1 - Nov 30, 10:00 to dusk. Side-by-sides prohibited (County by-law 3148). Opening date varies (e.g. May 4).
trails.notes: Possibly missing or unnamed in the app. This was not checked geometrically.

trails.name: Victoria Rail Trail (South Corridor named; North Corridor Fenelon - Kinmount unnamed in app)
trails.correct_class: MAYBE. North Corridor is UNSURE, and one segment in Fenelon Falls is NO.
trails.pass: KATVA permit required on city-owned trails
trails.notes: Fenelon Falls council banned motorized vehicles between Garnet Graham Park and Northline Road. OTN lists no ATV use on the North Corridor.

trails.name: Wollaston Township rail trail (Coe Hill Riders / OFATV)
trails.pass: OFATV permit (per the earlier survey). No source could be reached this session.
trails.notes: chatvc.ca was blocked and the web search found nothing.

trails.name: Lingham hydro line / Lingham Lake Road
trails.app_class: Lingham Lake Road: FREE 10 km (MNRF), MAYBE 9 km. Effingham-Grimsthorpe Hydroline Road Network: FREE 5.4 km.
trails.correct_class: FREE on Crown sections plausible; Hydro One corridor rules unknown
trails.pass: None found
trails.notes: Ontario's Lingham Lake CR statement says the utility corridor is 'traveled by ATVs and snowmobiles'. Inside the CR, ATVs are permitted only on existing trails. The conservation-authority trail to the dam from the north bars motorized vehicles. onX calls it Crown land plus utility right-of-way.

trails.name: OFSC-numbered trails classed FREE (OFSC 64: 12.2 km FREE; OFSC 62: 6.3 km FREE; also OFSC - B, OFSC - 11)
trails.pass: Not applicable. An OFSC permit is snowmobile-only.
trails.notes: OFSC's code of conduct says 'Do not ride an ATV on any OFSC trail at any time of year'. OFSC (2021) says trails on private property are winter snowmobile-only, and entering them is a chargeable trespass. Crown-land segments may be legal off-season under general Crown land rules, but they should not be shown as FREE.

trails.name: Barron Canyon Road
trails.pass: Not applicable
trails.notes: Ontario's Crown land FAQ excludes provincial parks from the general ORV permission. No source was found on ORVs on Algonquin's public access roads. The parts outside the park are a road-by-law question for the other agent.

trails.name: Opeongo Road
trails.pass: Not applicable on the road. The nearby RCATV 'Opeongo trail system' (Wilno - Madawaska) needs an OFATV/RCATV permit.

trails.name: IB & O Rail Trail
trails.pass: Unknown
trails.notes: The earlier survey says Ontario Trails Council lists it as an ATV trail (14 km). The reason given in the app ('private') is probably wrong; it is a municipal rail trail. This was not verified.

eota.pass_prices_2026: ATV or dirt bike: $150 season, $75 week, $25 day. Horse $75/$25/$7.50, bicycle $50/$20/$5, ski $35/$15/$3.50. Source: thetrail.ca/passes online form, read 2026-11-14. Bancroft's town page and 2022-2025 articles still say $20/day.
eota.how_to_buy: Online (PayPal; you get a numbered ID pass PDF, and weekly and annual passes are mailed) or from vendors in Bancroft (Bancroft Inn & Suites), Tweed (EOTA office), Cloyne, Havelock, Stirling, Belleville, Trenton, Napanee and others. Vendor headings also list Barry's Bay, Whitney, Wilno, Madawaska, Eganville, Killaloe, Golden Lake, Griffith, Pembroke and Petawawa.
eota.coverage: Hastings Heritage Trail (156 km, Glen Ross - Lake St. Peter), Trans Canada Trail across Hastings, and EOTA multi-use trails (E100/E102/E105, Egan Creek, Old Bessemer, Limerick, Weslemkoon, Coe Hill Siderail, Trail of Two Lakes and others per OTN). Network size is quoted as 700+ km (2025) up to about 2,700 km. OnePass partners: Park to Park, Napanee & District, Peterborough County Trails, Huron Shores and South Bruce Peninsula clubs (2020 infographic and the club list on EOTA's pass form). One article warns that EOTA's map shows some trails its pass does not cover.
eota.self_guided_loops: Four routes on thetrail.ca/the-trails: Central Hastings Heritage Loop (Tweed-Madoc-Marmora-Stirling), Tweed - Bancroft Route, Tweed - Flinton - Gilmour Loop (also called Tweed to Gunter Loop, which goes 'past Gunter to ... Bon Echo Provincial Park'), and Head North from Corbyville.
eota.ofatv_reciprocity: Partial. The Feb 2021 EOTA-OFATV MOU lets OFATV permit holders ride the Hastings County trails only (Hastings Heritage Trail and the Trans Canada rail trail across Hastings). It does not cover other EOTA trails. Destination Ontario lists the HHT pass as 'OnePass EOTA, OFATV'. No change to this was found. A 2024 Frontenac report says a general OFATV/EOTA reciprocal pass has still not been agreed.
eota.winter: The Limerick Lake page says wheeled vehicles are prohibited on the trail until the end of the 2025/26 snowmobile season; this is unconfirmed. EOTA's about page says 'When snow grooming is occurring ATV's with tracks are allowed only on the Eastern Ontario Trails Alliance's Trails', which is ambiguous.
eota.ofatv_price_2026: Unknown. ofatv.org was blocked and no search result gave a price. The earlier survey's $195/$175 is unverified.

ofsc_position.summary: ATVs may not use OFSC trails. Code of conduct item: 'Do not ride an ATV on any OFSC trail at any time of year'; an older pledge version says 'on private property'. OFSC press release (11 Mar 2021): 'OFSC trails on private property are for winter use only by snowmobiles. Illegally entering these closed snowmobile trails at any time is a chargeable act of trespass under Ontario law.' OFSC permits are sold only for MSVA-defined snowmobiles, not ATVs, SxS, snow bikes or Argos (OFSC FAQ). The 2022 OFSC-OFATV MOU addresses 'seasonal trail usage' and trespass. It does not open OFSC trails to ATVs.
ofsc_position.app_impact: OFSC-named segments (OFSC 64, OFSC 62 and others) are currently FREE where on Crown land. Reclassify them to at least MAYBE with a snowmobile-trail warning, and to NO in winter.

missing.name: Haliburton County Rail Trail (Kinmount - Haliburton)
missing.status: MAYBE: HATVA/KATVA permit, May 1 - Nov 30, no side-by-sides
missing.note: Not found by name in app geometry

missing.name: Haliburton Forest & Wild Life Reserve (private, about 100,000 acres)
missing.status: MAYBE/paid: permit required for all visitors (~$52/day per driver + HST, date unknown). The current policy page says ATVs are allowed only in winter on shared snowmobile trails, and side-by-sides and dirt bikes are not allowed. A 2018 doc allowed summer use on Class 1 roads.

missing.name: Conservation reserves with permitted ATV use on existing trails (e.g. Lingham Lake CR)
missing.status: The app's blanket rule 'no ORVs in provincial parks and conservation reserves' is too strict for CRs. Lingham Lake CR explicitly permits ATVs 'only on existing trails'. Each CR's management statement must be checked; provincial parks remain NO.

missing.name: Free Crown-land riding
missing.status: Already modelled: the app classes about 1,324 km of MNRF forest access roads as FREE. Ontario: ATVs are allowed on Crown land except parks and CRs unless restricted by planning or signs; registration, insurance and municipal by-laws still apply; May 1 is recommended to avoid spring damage.

missing.name: County forests near Bancroft that allow ATVs
missing.status: None found. No Hastings County forest-tract ATV areas were found. The Haliburton County Forest Conservation By-law (1999) exists, but its vehicle rules were not found. Northumberland County Forest has ATV trails but is outside or at the edge of the area.

missing.name: Name/attribution gaps (geometry present, pass status lost)
missing.status: Old Bessemer Trail (EOTA) is mapped as Bessemer Road / Egan Creek Road Network (FREE/ROAD). Limerick Trail is mapped as St. Ola Road. Egan Creek Trail is mapped as a T&C road. Joining on OTN would add the EOTA flag.

eco_loop.finding: No ATV route called 'Eco loop', 'Echo loop' or 'EOTA loop' exists in any source checked. That covers EOTA's site (all pages in its sitemap), the Town of Bancroft trail pages, Northern Ontario Travel and web search.
candidates: EOTA 'Tweed - Flinton - Gilmour Loop' (aka 'Tweed to Gunter Loop'). This is a real EOTA ATV self-guided loop whose description goes 'past Gunter to the magnificent Bon Echo Provincial Park'. It is the most likely ATV meaning of 'Echo loop'.
OFSC 'Bon Echo Loop' (about 232-257 km, staged from Bancroft or Cloyne, uses TOP E106/B106E on the HHT). This is SNOWMOBILE ONLY; ATVs are prohibited on OFSC trails.

'Central Ontario Loop Trail' (COLT, about 450 km through Hastings, Haliburton, Kawartha Lakes, Peterborough and Northumberland, using HHT, rail and ATV trails). The Town of Bancroft calls it 'the Central Ontario Loop trails ... open all year'. 'C.O. Loop' could be misheard as 'Eco loop'. It is a tourism/bikepacking route, not a single-pass ATV trail.
Big Rock Eco Retreat. This is Bancroft lodging that pairs with UTV tours, not a trail.
